notes.claim: When squaring a negative number on a calculator, brackets are needed to make the number negative before it is squared.
Writing negative numbers in brackets makes a calculation easier to read.
Absolute pressure is the sum of gauge pressure and atmospheric pressure, and a gauge reading below atmospheric is negative.
Change in velocity is final velocity minus initial velocity, and a slowing object's acceleration is negative.

sources.title: 11.6 Gauge Pressure, Absolute Pressure, and Pressure Measurement - College Physics 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: Gauge pressure is the pressure relative to atmospheric pressure. Gauge pressure is positive for pressures above atmospheric pressure, and negative for pressures below it.

sources.title: 11.6 Gauge Pressure, Absolute Pressure, and Pressure Measurement - College Physics 2e | OpenStax
sources.quote: Absolute pressure is the sum of gauge pressure and atmospheric pressure.

sources.title: Velocity and acceleration - Describing motion - AQA - GCSE Combined Science Revision - AQA Trilogy - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: change in velocity = final velocity - initial velocity

sources.title: Velocity and acceleration - Describing motion - AQA - GCSE Combined Science Revision - AQA Trilogy - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: If an object is slowing down, it is decelerating (and its acceleration has a negative value).

sources.title: How to multiply and divide positive and negative numbers – KS3 Maths – BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: Calculations can be written with brackets around negative numbers because this can make a calculation easier to read, eg -3 × -1 is the same calculation as (-3) × (-1)

sources.title: Squares, roots and powers: 1.2 Squaring fractions and negative numbers | OpenLearn - Open University
sources.quote: Brackets are needed to tell the calculator to make the 9 negative and then square

sources.title: Squares, roots and powers: 1.2 Squaring fractions and negative numbers | OpenLearn - Open University
